item.description:
First release of Shift.
- Run several coding tasks in parallel with Claude Code or Codex, each in its own Git worktree, branch and dev server. - Test each task in your browser, look at the diff, and merge into your base branch. - Answer agent questions and approvals from the app; get notified when a task is ready. - Push merged work to your remote.
- Signed and notarized by Apple: Shift now opens without a security warning. - The push button stays next to the task list when no task is selected.

- Attach files and images by dropping them on a prompt field. The agent gets their file paths. - App projects use a build command in place of a dev server. The task's Build button builds the app and opens it. - Drag projects in the sidebar to reorder them. - Right-click a project to open it in your editor or in Finder. - Task rows resize when the agent's description comes in. - Task list sections have more space between them. - Diff change counts use a smaller monospaced font.

- Drop any file on a prompt to attach it, and paste images or files straight from the clipboard - See how much of Claude Code's or Codex's usage limit you have left in the bottom bar - Switching a project to App build fills in its build command for you - ⌘, opens the current project's settings - "Open in" menus show Finder once and now include Terminal - Project icons show up for more projects, including Icon Composer icons and monorepos - Task rows are all the same height - The project title in the task list resizes to fit when you switch projects

- Drop any file on a prompt to attach it, and paste images or files straight from the clipboard - See how much of Claude Code's or Codex's usage limit you have left in the bottom bar - Switching a project to App build fills in its build command for you - ⌘, opens the current project's settings - "Open in" menus show Finder once and now include Terminal - Project icons show up for more projects, including Icon Composer icons and monorepos - Task rows are all the same height - The project title in the task list resizes to fit when you switch projects

- Pick the model for Claude Code or Codex in project settings or the bottom bar - Each task keeps its own base branch, and changing it moves only that task's work - Create a new branch from the base picker with New Branch… - Push a task's branch to origin from the More menu, or automatically when it finishes - Agent output is readable now, with a Raw toggle for the original stream - Your new task draft stays put when a task finishes or moves to another section - Merging no longer deletes work when a task's base is set to its own branch

- The server link shows Starting, Running, Not responding or Stopped, based on whether the server actually answers. - A server that stops responding offers Log and Restart, and logs open scrolled to the end. - The globe shows a spinner while the base server starts, and opens the browser once the server is ready. - If a server ends up on a different address, the globe opens that one, or tells you the server did not start. - Adding a folder that is not a Git repository offers to initialize Git for you. - Server, merge and task action buttons are taller, with rounded corners.

- Unsent text in the new task field is kept per project. Switching projects shows a blank field, and coming back brings your draft and attachments back. - Each task keeps its own unsent prompt or answer when you switch to another task. - The suggested dev server command now gives Vite and Astro projects their task's port.

- If another app is already using a task's server port, the server moves to a free port. - When an agent creates a project in an empty folder, its dev server starts automatically and runs `npm install` first if it needs to. - Each server start begins with an empty log. - Follow-up prompts no longer change a task's title and description, which stay about the whole task. - Prompt history shows your newest prompts first. - Image attachments appear as thumbnails. Hover over one to see its name and a remove button.

- Share task dev servers on your tailnet: if Tailscale is installed, a Tailscale button appears next to the localhost link - When you hit a usage limit, a countdown shows when it resets and the task continues automatically - Re-sync a task with its base branch from the More menu. If there's a conflict, choose to fix it with the agent, view the diff or undo - Open a pull request from the merge button's dropdown - Conflicted tasks list the files that conflict - Click a changed file to open the diff at that file - See the server's reason when a push is rejected - The branch name now shows next to the localhost button

- Choose a project type in Settings (static website, dynamic website, native app, Electron app, or other), detected automatically when you add a project - Run Electron apps from a task with a Run/Stop button, with copies from several tasks running side by side - Pick Localhost or Tailscale from a single server button that remembers your choice - See a task's branch in its top bar and click to copy it - Click anywhere on the chevron side of a split button to open its menu - Read command fields in Settings more easily in a monospaced font

- Chat with each project in a new pinned Chat row: one read-only conversation for questions and planning that picks up where you left off - See what the agent did on each task with the new Agent view, which shows one turn at a time with tool steps collapsed into a short summary - Set up a native app project before it has a build command; Build works out what to run, or tells you there's nothing to build yet - Create a new folder when adding a project - Click the branch on a task to copy its name - Task actions now appear in a clearer order: merge, Tailscale, server, branch

- Project chat can now edit files, use git and run scripts in the project's folder, following the project's permission setting, with Allow and Deny in the chat for manual projects - Open the agent's reply by clicking anywhere on a prompt, replacing the Prompts/Agent tabs - Push merges in what the remote has and pushes again instead of failing, and tells you if conflicts or uncommitted changes get in the way - Stop a running task from its button row - Change the base branch, re-sync it and push the task branch from the merge dropdown, including when a task has conflicts - Open the server log in its own window that follows the output, and restart the server from the server dropdown, now shown without Tailscale too - Launching Shift no longer starts every web project's server; a project's server starts only when you open it, and a project whose folder is gone says so plainly

- Chat with your project to start, follow, message, stop, merge and delete tasks, and to read or change project settings - Follow a task's pull request: view it, push new work to it, and finish the task when it's merged - Pre-fill pull request titles and descriptions, and optionally open pull requests from a task's main button - Add optional before and after screenshots of your changes for web projects - Rename tasks from the More menu or the task list, and keep a running description of each task's changes - Open the latest prompt's output automatically as you work through a conversation - Render markdown tables as tables in conversations - Stop showing routine step failures as red warnings in conversations

- Follow and steer tasks from your iPhone with the new iOS companion app: pair by QR code over Tailscale, see conversations, approve or deny requests, stop or resume tasks, and preview dev servers - Give a project several build targets, such as a Mac app, iOS Simulator, run command or script, each with its own build state and logs - Choose a target from the Build button, which becomes a split button with several targets and suggests the one that covers most of the task's changes - Let Shift detect build targets automatically, or edit them in project settings or through the chat - Your Mac stays awake while a task is working, and you can revoke a paired phone at any time

- Dev servers no longer fail with "port in use" when Tailscale is sharing that port, and a server that loses its port moves to a free one - Your messages have a lighter background - Empty states look cleaner - The screenshots setting is always visible and explains when it's unavailable

- Agents take screenshots that show the actual change, including after a click or with a modal open, with up to 4 shots per task - Screenshots now work for app projects: the agent builds and runs the app, then captures the view that changed - Screenshot thumbnails show as a stack that spreads out when you click it - Clicking Chat focuses its prompt field - Chat's Working status and Stop button share a row above the prompt
- Dev servers that only listen on IPv6 localhost, like Astro, now load on the phone - Select text across paragraphs, headings and list items in the chat - A smaller folder icon in the project list

- Task servers start only when you open a task, on your Mac or your phone, or when its agent runs. Servers no one has used for 30 minutes stop on their own. - Turn off a web project's servers from its menu in the sidebar - Running agents keep going when the internet drops: Shift shows that it can't connect and continues the turn once you're back online - See thumbnails of added and changed images in file diffs. Click one to open it in Quick Look. - A bar now sits behind New Project when the projects list scrolls under it, and the project footer lines up with it - The pointer turns into a hand over links in messages

- Each task keeps the agent, model and permissions it started with. Changing the project's settings no longer changes your open tasks, and you can switch a task's agent from the footer. - Settings (⌘,) now holds your editor, terminal, idle server timeout and paired devices. Project Settings moves to ⇧⌘,. - Opening a task no longer starts its server, and idle servers stop after 5 minutes by default. The server dot shows gray, yellow or green. - New keyboard shortcuts: ⌘R runs or opens the preview, ⌘. stops the app, ⇧⌘E opens your editor, ⇧⌘O shows the folder in Finder. There are also shortcuts to switch projects and tasks, search, message the agent, copy the preview link and open in the terminal. - The Open in menu lists your editor and terminal first, with their app icons. Other apps are under Open in Other. - Make text bigger or smaller with ⌘+, ⌘− and ⌘0 in the conversation, prompts, diff and the agent's questions. - The pull request badge is green while a pull request is open and grey once it's merged. Push Changes sends new work to an open pull request. - Right-click a task in the list for the same actions as the More menu. The branch button shows the task's base branch, like main ← shift/3018.

- Type `/task` followed by a prompt in a task or the project chat to start a new task in the same project - Easier-to-read text across the app: no more tiny labels, and stronger contrast on task numbers, branch names and usage limits - Chat replies are easier to read, with more space between lines and paragraphs and inline code that matches the size of the text around it - Paired phones stay connected after Shift updates or restarts, so you don't have to pair them again

- Select text across paragraphs, headings and list items in a message in one go - Prompts stand out more, with replies indented under them, and headings, bold text and lists are easier to read - Hide the sidebar from View › Hide Sidebar or with ⌃⌘S - The pointer turns into a hand over links in messages - List markers sit next to their text, and wrapped lines line up under it - Headings after a table or code block get the same space above them as after a paragraph

- A warning in the sidebar shows which project's tasks are using a lot of memory: 2 GB or more, or 1 GB when the Mac is low on memory - A new memory window, like Force Quit, lists each project's running tasks and servers, so you can stop one or all of them - A notification banner now appears every time a task finishes, not just the first time - Notifications show the project name as the title and say whether a task is ready for review or needs your attention - Press ⇧⌘G to open the project's GitHub repository - Long repository paths in the project bar now cut off the start instead of the end, so the end of the path stays visible

- Empty projects pick up their project type once code lands on main - Starting a new task from an empty main branch now shows a warning - Permissions now appear below Default agent and Model in the Agent settings - Prompt text uses a regular font weight - Messages stay wrapped to their width when you expand steps
